definition: Field dependence is a cognitive style in which a person’s attention and reasoning are more shaped by surrounding information, making them more likely to shift focus with changes in the task context. In this packet, field-dependent individuals showed less stable attention allocation and greater base-rate neglect than field-independent individuals during Bayesian reasoning tasks.
